summary: Cow Head's 1909 cast-iron light, kept by the Payne family, was switched off in 1979 or 1988 and restored in 2002; it is now a municipal heritage building.

structures.note: 5.5 m (18 ft) per Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett; register: 5 m to balcony, 8 m to vane; register also calls the tower steel plate in its character list.

staffing.note: Battery operated from 1978 (Lighthouse Friends); register says operation ended 1979.

access.note: Town-owned, inside Gros Morne National Park (register). Site and tower open (Rowlett, Lighthouse Friends). Route: road west from Route 430 into the town, then across the isthmus. Lighthouse Trail easy 1.5 km loop, about 45 minutes.

keepers.name: Jesse Payne
keepers.note: First keeper (register). Lit the kerosene lamp at dusk and put it out at dawn, spring to late December. Start year inferred from 1909 activation; death date not given.

keepers.name: John L. Payne (Lighthouse Jack)
keepers.note: Son of Jesse Payne. Lighthouse Friends gives 1949 to at least 1953. Wages cut after the 1952 acetylene change; moved to Tuckers Cove (Lighthouse Friends).

keepers.name: Jesse Payne (grandson)
keepers.note: Named in the register as the grandson who was a lightkeeper. Lighthouse Friends calls the final keeper 'Jesse Payne, son of Lighthouse Jack'. Dates not given. Not joined to the first keeper of the same name. Connection ended after 1960: named only as published.

corrections.current: 1905 built (Year of the tower described by the Lighthouse Directory)
corrections.why: Rowlett alone gives 1905. The register and Lighthouse Friends both date the tower to 1909 (Lighthouse Friends: erected 1908, activated 1909). The Rowlett 1905 date is uncorroborated.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett put the light out of use in 1988; the register says it guided ships until 1979. The sources differ on the year, but all say it no longer operates; the record's inactive status stands.
Lighthouse Friends calls the final keeper Jesse Payne, son of Lighthouse Jack; the register calls him grandson. The register's family line is followed in the story and the roster.

notes_for_editor: THIN STATION: four web sources only; no corpus or newspaper material (Newfoundland is outside the Canadian Department of Marine corpus, which runs 1900-1924, and Chronicling America is US-only). No storms or wrecks are sourced for the light, so that chapter is omitted. DATE OF BUILD: Rowlett 1905; Lighthouse Friends erected 1908, activated 1909; register 1909; the record says 1905 from Rowlett. The story uses 1909. END OF SERVICE: Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett say 1988 (discontinued by Transport Canada); the register says the light guided ships until 1979 (battery harbour buoys replaced it). Lighthouse Friends says battery operation began in 1978. The story gives both. LIGHT CHARACTERISTIC: Lighthouse Friends says fixed white, focal height 141 ft (43 m), range fifteen miles; the Heritage NL note says ten one-second flashes a minute and a range of 22.5 km. The record's 'F W' follows Lighthouse Friends and is not verified by a list of lights (the Canadian Coast Guard list was not checked for this station; Lighthouse Friends' 'inactive' note suggests it is no longer listed). Range was not converted to nautical miles because the units are not clear in either source. TOWER MATERIAL: register says cast iron in one passage and steel plate in another; Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett say cast iron. TOWER HEIGHT: Lighthouse Friends 18 ft (5.5 m); Rowlett 5 m (18 ft); register 5 m to balcony and 8 m to vane. PAINT: Lighthouse Friends red and white stripes, lantern white; Rowlett white with red trim; repainted solid white in 1978 per Lighthouse Friends; repainted 2019 per Rowlett. KEEPERS: first keeper Jesse Payne has no dates beyond 'first' (register) and his death is not dated (Lighthouse Friends). Lighthouse Friends says his son John L. was keeper after Jesse died, and gives 1949 to at least 1953. The grandson (register) and 'Jesse Payne, son of Lighthouse Jack' (Lighthouse Friends) are not joined to the first keeper. Lighthouse Friends' first-keeper house is 'three bedroom'; the register says 'three room'. Sources have not been checked for the 1952 keeper's name or dates beyond Lighthouse Friends' list. LIVING PEOPLE: Jesse Payne (grandson) and John L. Payne are named only as sources name them, with no personal detail beyond the family line. NOT READ: the Canadian Register page historicplaces.ca/en/rep-reg/place-lieu.aspx?id=3840 (fetch returned no text; the Heritage Guide copy of the same register entry was used); the Virtual Museum Canada page cited by Lighthouse Friends; the ACOA 2001 release; Town of Cow Head records. CHECKED 2026-10-27: the whole Lighthouse Friends page was read. Corrections: LF says 'iron tower', not cast iron (the register's cast-iron and steel-plate wording conflict is left in the notes, not the story); the fixed white light and 43 m (141 ft) height are LF's; the 2001 funding programme is the Canada-Newfoundland Comprehensive Economic Development Agreement, for tourism infrastructure. LF's 'work as a fisherman while still keeping an eye on the light' replaces 'fish'. The first quotation check on this station ran after the evidence additions; the result (0 missing across all 55 quotes) includes both the original and the added quotes. The distance of fifteen miles has no unit in LF and is marked so in the story.
